Small triplets trigger more showers: at N = 99, 48% (r = 10 m) vs 35% grid · N = 48: 30% vs 15% · N = 21: 14% vs 4%
one triangle a few tens of metres across can supply all 3 detectors > 1 particle on its own
But they point worse: within 1° with the trigger, N = 99: 3.0–3.9% (r ≤ 200 m) vs grid 4.7%, best disk (4.5 km) 6.1%
among triggered showers the median error is 4.2° (r = 10 m) vs 2.6° (grid): the short baseline can't fix the direction

Large triplets (r = 500 m) are just a spread-out layout: 5.0% vs grid 4.7% within 1° at N = 99; still below the best disk
No trigger: small triplets lose (N = 99: 4.7–7.6% vs grid 9.7%, best disk 11.6%) — fewer independent sampling points
Triplets beat the 2 / 4 / 5-detector clusters at the same r (more cluster centres for the same N → more area)
Background: no change up to 1 µs; at 10 µs everything collapses (recon trained without noise), triplets included
Caveat: r = 10 / 25 m is below the training zoo's cluster radii (30–600 m), so the recon is extrapolating there
Verdict: triplets help detection (trigger), not 1° pointing · coverage (grid / disk) still wins at 1°
